text.p: Some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Saab Automobile president Bob Hendry says the company will not produce a third model to complement the 900 series and the 9000 series, which is soon to be replaced.

- The battle for telecoms customers in the Nordic region is heating up. Sweden's Telia has started a price war with Denmark's TeleDanmark for Danish subscribers and the Kinnevik-owned Tele2 has entered the fray.
- Sweden's Centre Party, which has entered an informal alliance on economic matters with the ruling Social Democrats, has not abandoned its aim of phasing out nuclear power by 2010.

- A new major player is set to enter the Swedish stock market. Sven Benestam, head of public sector pension fund FSO, says he will invest 500 million crowns in Swedish shares annually, although he is waiting for a correction of the current rally.
- The Stockholm Stock Exchange's plans to enable major players to buy and sell shares direct and bypass the stockbroker lead has been met with a chilly reception.
